title: How ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’ Makes Billions From ‘Free’ Loans | WSJ The Economics Of
summary: WSJ explainer on how BNPL providers make money despite offering zero-interest loans, covering fees, risk, and regulation.

assertions.quote: the lion's share of our income, 90-plus percent of our income, is made from the merchant, not the consumer
a quarter of BNPL customers have used them to buy groceries, up from 14% in 2024
more than two-thirds of BNPL loans went to borrowers with lower credit scores
41% of BNPL users paid late in the past year, up from 34% a year before
about 20% of our business today is 0%, and about 80% has interest on them
President Trump and DOGE have since crippled the Consumer Protection Agency

verdicts.note: Multiple reports describe the CFPB withdrawing its interpretive rule and reducing enforcement capacity in 2025.
KC Fed: the CFPB has signaled its plan to revoke the May 2024 interpretive rule that extended dispute/refund protections to BNPL, consistent with weakening oversight.

assertions.quote: FICO announced in June that it would add buy now, pay later loans to credit report

verdicts.note: Affirm reports to Experian and TransUnion, FICO built a scoring model incorporating the data, though adoption is still uneven.
KC Fed endnote: some BNPL providers partner with credit bureaus to submit eligible users' repayment behavior to help build their credit files, e.g. Sezzle's TransUnion partnership.
